component.name: Kempt
component.summary: One-click system updates with a truthful badge

description.p: Kempt is a Plasma 6 panel widget and a bash command-line tool that shows exactly which system updates are pending, counts only the ones you have not held, and applies them with one click from the panel.
The badge and the update come from the same command path, so they cannot disagree.

ul.li: dnf5 and Flatpak updates, with the version each package moves from and to.
Holds that skip a package but keep reporting it.
Offline staging for updates that could disturb the running session.

screenshot.caption: Kempt in the system tray, with the pending-updates popup open
The settings page: run surface, check interval, restart reminders and the password-prompt controls

description.p: A machine a long way behind now updates: past about nine hundred pending packages the check used to fail and the panel blamed a missing installation. Kempt refuses to stage updates over a stored Fedora release upgrade, because staging would cancel the upgrade, and refuses to update an image-based Fedora, where rpm-ostree or bootc rather than dnf is what updates the system.

A hold added after an offline update was staged is no longer silent, in the command line or the popup. The panel widget is now its own package, kempt-plasmoid, so the command line no longer pulls in a desktop. Three ways a staged update could quietly stop being real are now caught and announced.
A widget installed before the CLI now walks you through installing the engine, with a Copy Commands button; kempt doctor catches a store copy shadowing the packaged widget.
